speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: asked	the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) from 2013 to 2015, how many eligible working fathers have applied for a full week of paid paternity leave; and (b) how many employers have agreed to provide an additional week of paid paternity leave since the initiative was announced at the National Day Rally in August 2015.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The number is small, as the scheme started only on 1 May 2013.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The enhanced paternity leave was announced at the National Day Rally in August 2015.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The statistics on the take-up of this leave enhancement will be available after that.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Page: 13 With the additional week of paternity leave granted, fathers can have more opportunities to spend with their children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I think it is also important for their marriage to allow both parents, the fathers and mothers, to not only enjoy the joys of parenthood but also to partake in the responsibilities of bringing up the child.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, 12,300 was the number for last year, 2015.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: When we compare this, there are probably 30,000 to 40,000 births each year.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: It looks like a very small number have taken this up.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Is it a case where the fathers who are eligible are not applying, or is it a case where the employers or organisations are not supportive?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: To add to that, as with many new policies, we expect the Government to take the lead.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, I would like to ask whether the Minister could share what is the take-up rate in the Civil Service, in particular.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do expect to see those numbers increase.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is a very good question: why are the fathers not applying?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We should ask the fathers why they are not doing so.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We all recognise that both parents, that is, fathers and mothers, play a very important part.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Why we took this step to introduce this is really to encourage both parents to take up a more active responsibility.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do very much encourage employers to do so.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do encourage our civil servants who do want to apply and we will be quite happy to support them.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Anecdotally, we do see a lot more feedback, certainly in terms of younger fathers, playing a much more active role in a range of different areas.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: On this leave front, we would very much like to see the numbers increase as well.
